preview: Interview experience of Vedant Mondkar for the Summer Intern – Software Development role at Hilti Technology Solutions India (HTSI) in 2021.
content:
HTSI(Hilti Technology Solutions India)
Role: Summer Intern – Software Development
Vedant Mondkar | VJTI B.Tech. IT’23
HTSI:
Hilti Technology Solutions India(HTSI) is a technology & innovation driven construction
solutions company, located in Pune. The Hilti group was founded in 1941 at Schaan,
Liechtenstein. Today, it has over 30k+ employees in 120+ countries., with 250k+
customer contacts daily. Ranked 14th in Europe & 22nd in World as Best Multinational
Workplace.Company provides system Solutions,software solutions as well as services
for construction Professionals.
HTSI visited our campus on 28 September ,2021 for the On-Campus Internship Drive.
Eligibility: 6+ CGPA
Branches:
Computer Engineering , Information Technology ,Electronics & Telecommunication ,
Electronics Engineering ,Electrical Engineering , Mechanical Engineering
The special thing was that HTSI visited VJTI campus for the first time for interns as well
as full time hiring.
The company had kept pre-placement talk just before the online test,i.e. at 4pm. It is
always advisable to pay close attention in pre placement talks and to take screenshots
of the slides (In our case everything was online hence screenshots :P).
Try to make short notes from the points in those slides  which can help you later during
interview rounds (Specially final round)

Rounds
1) Online Test - 1st October
2) Technical Interview - 2nd October
3) HR Interview - 2nd October

Online Test-
Online Test was scheduled at 6pm on the same day, 1st Oct,2021. It was conducted on
the mercer mettl platform.
The proctor was strict, even if pop-ups appear test can be closed immediately without
any warning(so take all necessary precautions beforehand :P)
Around 250+ students had registered for the online Test.The duration of the test was 90
minutes.
The test was exhaustive with nearly everything covered. It consisted of 61 questions
with 7 sections:
DSA and coding(1 Q)
Aptitude and reasoning questions(30 MCQs)
Data structure MCQs
SQL MCQs
OS MCQs
OOPS MCQs
Computer Networks MCQs
Each of the CS subjects MCQs were around 6-7.
There were no individual time limits on the sections except for the Aptitude and
Reasoning section where 30MCQs had to be solved in 30 mins.
The coding question was like this:
Convert the given array to an array having unique elements by increasing the value of
each element such that it is unique from elements appearing before it.
Testcase1:
6
2 2 1 3 4 4
O/p: 2 3 1 4 5 6
Testcase2:
7
1 2 2 6 1 3 2
O/p: 1 2 3 6 4 5 7

The coding question was of easy to medium level and could be easily solved using set
library in C++.
The shortlist came at 11am on the next day. I had performed pretty well in the test and
as a result I was one among the 30 students shortlisted for interview rounds.

Technical Round:(25 minutes)
As the company came for hiring for the first time in VJTI as well as India, we were not
having any of our seniors' experience. I searched on gfg as well but no interview
experiences were available for HTSI.
Still I revised OS, DBMS, OOPS on the day of interview as the interview were going to
start at 4pm , 2nd Oct, 2021, on Microsoft Teams.
My Round 1 was scheduled at 7pm:
● The interview started with the standard question of tell me about yourself, after
that he asked me about what technologies I am familiar with. I briefed him about
the languages and technologies I know.
● Then he asked me one typical HR question, which was what are your future
goals, to which I replied firmly, as I was already prepared. I briefed him about my
short as well as long term goals.
● Then he shifted to a puzzle cum coding question:
An input sequence as well as output sequence was given. I had to find the
logic behind the generation of o/p seq from i/p sequence.
He first gave me example:
input->{12,70,7,44,9,1}
output->{8,21,114}
After 2 mins of thinking I wasn't able to conclude anything, I immediately asked
for another example(don’t be shy to ask for a hint, be interactive). He gave me
next example:
input-> {123,331,23,90,15,61}
output-> {38,151,454}
Even now I was not getting the logic, but don’t let the interviewer know that you
are confused, just keep calm. I told just one thing that the o/p sequence length is
half of that i/p sequence. (Always tell the interviewer whatever you have found till
now, don’t stay quiet, it helps interviewer to understand about your progress
towards solving problem)
After that i told him that we have to find relations between pairs to get the o/p
sequence, he said yes, going in the right direction. Soon, i got the logic that
subtracting one number from other works here, I told him this.After which i was
able to conclude that sorting the array and subtracting adjacent numbers work
here.
He said my approach was correct and asked me to code it.
I coded it and runned to on above test cases and passed them without any error.
Then he asked me if I had any questions for me, I asked him two. (Always ask
questions as it shows your interest in company)
The interview lasted around 25 mins
After this, immediately I came to know that I was selected for the next round.Total
16 students out of 30 in first were shortlisted for the second round.

HR Round:
The HR round is to judge your personality, what you know about the company
and your compatibility for the role.
The round was scheduled at 7:40pm. The interviewer started with his
introduction. He was very friendly. Always, try to have a smile on your face while
talking with the interviewer, this round should feel like a conversation to both.
He was speaking from Malaysia, as he was doing WFH.
● He then asked me to introduce myself.
● Then he asked me why I wanted to join the company and what I know
about it?(those points noted came in handy:P)
● Next he asked, why I chose software engineering and what I like about it?
At last, he asked me if I had any questions for me, I asked him two.
The round lasted for around 20 minutes.

On the next day at 5 pm the results were announced, 8 students were offered
for the role of software developer intern and I was fortunate to be one of them.

Resources:
● For DSA, I have used 450dsa, InterviewBit, GeeksforGeeks, and
LeetCode. You can use Interviewbit and 450dsa for topic-wise questions.
GeeksforGeeks can be used for theory-related questions and you can also
practice previous year questions of companies. You can use LeetCode to
solve the most commonly asked interview questions.
● For revising C++, this is a good resource:
https://www.javatpoint.com/cpp-tutorial
● For revising OOPS, I referred:
https://www.javatpoint.com/cpp-oops-concepts
https://medium.com/@punitkmr/real-world-examples-for-oop-concepts-abb
9475b2095
Always, try to have at least one real world example of each pillar of oops.
● For revising OS, I referred:
https://www.tutorialspoint.com/operating_system/index.htm
● For revising DBMS, I referred to interviewbit,Tutorialspoint, and Javatpoint.
You can also use Hackerrank for SQL query practice.
● For Computer Network, I have used Love Babbar CheatSheet, and Gate
Smashers CN Playlist. Mostly, companies don’t ask questions on CN but
for preparation, you can use these resources.(Specially those companies
which come after MST)
● For Low level system design, I referred to Soumyajit Bhattacharya’s
Playlist, you can even refer to Gaurav Sen’s playlist.
● For HR interviews, find the most asked HR questions from various sites
like ,interviewbit, indiabix, prepare your own answers for experience based
questions, by recollecting your past memories.
